short: An Ancient Greek pre-Socratic philosopher primarily remembered for his atomic theory.
full:
Democritus was an Ancient Greek pre-Socratic philosopher from Abdera, primarily remembered today for his formulation of an atomic theory of the universe. Building on the ideas of his teacher Leucippus, he proposed that everything in the world was composed of small, indivisible, and indestructible particles called atoms, which move through a vast void. His theories were remarkably prescient, anticipating modern scientific conceptions of matter by over two millennia.

Beyond atomism, Democritus was a polymath who wrote extensively on ethics, physics, mathematics, music, and cosmology. He believed that the universe operates according to mechanical laws without the need for divine purpose or intervention. Though his works have largely been lost and are known mostly through second-hand reports by later philosophers like Aristotle, his materialist philosophy provided a crucial alternative to the teleological views that would later dominate Greek thought.
